column1: It’s time to start returning vanished native animals to Britain, says John Vesty
column2: 约翰·韦斯蒂说，是时候开始让已经消失的本土动物重返英国了。

column1: There is a poem, written around 598 AD, which describes hunting a mystery animal called a llewyn.
column2: 一首大约写于公元598年的诗，描写了猎捕一种名叫llewyn的神秘动物的情形。

column1: But what was it?
column2: 可它究竟是什么呢？
column4: what was it|它究竟是什么

column1: Nothing seemed to fit, until 2006, when an animal bone, dating from around the same period, was found in the Kinsey Cave in northern England.
column2: 似乎没有哪种动物对得上。直到2006年，人们在英格兰北部的金西洞穴中发现了一块约与这首诗同时期的动物骨骼。
column3: seemed to fit|似乎符合描述

column1: Until this discovery, the lynx — a large spotted cat with tasselled ears — was presumed to have died out in Britain at least 6,000 years ago, before the inhabitants of these islands took up farming.
column2: 在这项发现之前，人们以为猞猁——一种身有斑点、耳尖长着簇毛的大型猫科动物——至少在6000年前就已在英国消失，那时群岛居民尚未开始务农。
column4: spotted cat|身有斑点的猫科动物

column1: But the 2006 find, together with three others in Yorkshire and Scotland, is compelling evidence that the lynx and the mysterious llewyn were in fact one and the same animal.
column2: 但2006年的这项发现，加上约克郡和苏格兰的另外三项发现，构成了有力证据，表明猞猁和神秘的llewyn其实就是同一种动物。
column7: one and the same|完全相同的

column1: If this is so, it would bring forward the tassel-eared cat’s estimated extinction date by roughly 5,000 years.
column2: 如果确实如此，这种耳尖带簇毛的猫科动物在英国灭绝的估计时间，就要比原先认为的晚大约5000年。
column3: If this is so|如果确实如此
column4: bring forward|在这里指把年代移近今天
column6: estimated extinction date|估计的灭绝时间

column1: However, this is not quite the last glimpse of the animal in British culture.
column2: 不过，这还算不上这种动物在英国文化中最后一次留下踪影。

column1: A 9th-century stone cross from the Isle of Eigg shows, alongside the deer, boar and aurochs pursued by a mounted hunter, a speckled cat with tasselled ears.
column2: 埃格岛一座9世纪的石十字架上，刻着一个骑马的猎人追逐鹿、野猪和原牛；旁边还有一只带斑点、耳尖有簇毛的猫科动物。

column1: Were it not for the animal’s backside having worn away with time, we could have been certain, as the lynx’s stubby tail is unmistakable.
column2: 要不是石刻上动物的后半身已随岁月磨蚀，我们本来就能确定它的身份，因为猞猁短粗的尾巴很好辨认。
column3: Were it not for|要不是因为

column1: But even without this key feature, it’s hard to see what else the creature could have been.
column2: 不过，即使缺了这个关键特征，也很难想象这会是什么别的动物。

column1: The lynx is now becoming the totemic animal of a movement that is transforming British environmentalism: rewilding.
column2: 猞猁眼下正成为一场运动的象征。这场“再野化”运动正在改变英国的环保理念。
column3: totemic animal|具有象征意义的动物

column1: Rewilding means the mass restoration of damaged ecosystems.
column2: 再野化，就是大规模恢复受损的生态系统。

column1: It involves letting trees return to places that have been denuded, allowing parts of the seabed to recover from trawling and dredging, permitting rivers to flow freely again.
column2: 它包括让树木回到那些植被已被清除的地方，让部分海床从拖网捕捞和疏浚造成的破坏中恢复，让河流重新自由流淌。

column1: Above all, it means bringing back missing species.
column2: 最重要的是，让已经消失的物种重新回来。
column5: missing species|当地已消失的物种

column1: One of the most striking findings of modern ecology is that ecosystems without large predators behave in completely different ways from those that retain them.
column2: 现代生态学最引人注目的发现之一，是失去大型捕食者的生态系统，与那些仍有大型捕食者的生态系统，运作方式截然不同。

column1: Some of them drive dynamic processes that resonate through the whole food chain, creating niches for hundreds of species that might otherwise struggle to survive.
column2: 有些大型捕食者推动着影响遍及整个食物链的动态过程，为数百个原本可能难以生存的物种创造了生态位。

column1: The killers turn out to be bringers of life.
column2: 这些猎杀其他动物的捕食者，原来也能带来生机。
column4: turn out to be|结果表明是

column1: Such findings present a big challenge to British conservation, which has often selected arbitrary assemblages of plants and animals and sought, at great effort and expense, to prevent them from changing.
column2: 这类发现对英国的自然保护做法提出了重大挑战。以往，人们常任意选定一些动植物的组合，再耗费巨量人力物力，力求不让这些组合发生变化。
column6: at great effort and expense|耗费大量人力物力

column1: It has tried to preserve the living world as if it were a jar of pickles, letting nothing in and nothing out, keeping nature in a state of arrested development.
column2: 以往的做法试图像保存一罐腌菜一样保存生物世界：什么都不让进，什么都不让出，把自然维持在停滞不前的状态。
column5: a jar of pickles|一罐腌菜

column1: But ecosystems are not merely collections of species; they are also the dynamic and ever-shifting relationships between them.
column2: 然而，生态系统不仅是物种的集合，也包括物种之间活跃且不断变化的关系。

column1: And this dynamism often depends on large predators.
column2: 这种动态变化又往往取决于大型捕食者。

column1: At sea the potential is even greater: by protecting large areas from commercial fishing, we could once more see what 18th-century literature describes: vast shoals of fish being chased by fin and sperm whales, within sight of the English shore.
column2: 在海上，再野化的潜力甚至更大。如果保护大片海域，使其免受商业捕捞的影响，或许就能再现18世纪文献所描述的景象：站在英格兰海岸就看得见长须鲸和抹香鲸追赶着庞大的鱼群。
column7: vast shoals of fish|庞大的鱼群
column8: fin and sperm whales|长须鲸和抹香鲸
column9: within sight of|在……目力所及范围内

column1: This policy would also greatly boost catches in the surrounding seas; the fishing industry’s insistence on scouring every inch of seabed, leaving no breeding reserves, could not be more damaging to its own interests.
column2: 这项政策也会显著增加周边海域的渔获量。渔业从业者坚持将每寸海床都扫过，不留下繁殖保护区，最损害的恰是他们自己的利益。

column1: Rewilding is a rare example of an environmental movement in which campaigners articulate what they are for rather than only what they are against.
column2: 再野化是一场少见的环保运动：倡导者明确说出了自己支持什么，而不只是表明反对什么。
column7: what they are for|他们所支持的事

column1: One of the reasons why the enthusiasm for rewilding is spreading so quickly in Britain is that it helps to create a more inspiring vision than the green movement’s usual promise of ‘Follow us and the world will be slightly less awful than it would otherwise have been’.
column2: 英国人对再野化的热情之所以传播得这样快，一个原因是它描绘的愿景比环保运动通常作出的承诺更能鼓舞人。那种惯常的承诺是：“跟着我们走，世界就会比原本可能的样子少糟糕那么一点。”
column8: slightly less awful|稍微没那么糟

column1: The lynx presents no threat to human beings: there is no known instance of one preying on people.
column2: 猞猁对人没有威胁。目前尚无猞猁捕食人类的已知实例。

column1: It is a specialist predator of roe deer, a species that has exploded in Britain in recent decades, holding back, by intensive browsing, attempts to re-establish forests.
column2: 猞猁专门捕食狍。近几十年英国的狍数量暴增，它们大量啃食枝叶，阻碍了人们恢复森林的努力。
column3: specialist predator|专以某种猎物为食的捕食者

column1: It will also winkle out sika deer: an exotic species that is almost impossible for human beings to control, as it hides in impenetrable plantations of young trees.
column2: 猞猁还会把梅花鹿从藏身处赶出来。梅花鹿是外来物种，躲在密得难以穿行的幼林中，人类几乎无法控制它们。

column1: The attempt to reintroduce this predator marries well with the aim of bringing forests back to parts of our bare and barren uplands.
column2: 重新引入猞猁这一捕食者，与在部分光秃荒凉的高地恢复森林的目标十分契合。

column1: The lynx requires deep cover, and as such presents little risk to sheep and other livestock, which are supposed, as a condition of farm subsidies, to be kept out of the woods.
column2: 猞猁需要茂密植被的掩护，因此对羊和其他牲畜威胁很小。农业补贴本来也有一项条件，即牲畜应被挡在林地之外。
column6: as a condition of|作为……的条件
column8: kept out of the woods|不让进入林地

column1: On a recent trip to the Cairngorm Mountains, I heard several conservationists suggest that the lynx could be reintroduced there within 20 years.
column2: 前不久我去凯恩戈姆山脉，听到几位自然保护人士提出，猞猁有可能在20年内被重新引入那里。

column1: If trees return to the bare hills elsewhere in Britain, the big cats could soon follow.
column2: 如果英国其他地方的荒山重新长出树木，这些大型猫科动物也可能很快跟着回来。
column6: could soon follow|可能不久也会到来

column1: There is nothing extraordinary about these proposals, seen from the perspective of anywhere else in Europe.
column2: 从欧洲其他地方的角度看，这些提议并没有什么非同寻常。
column5: from the perspective of|从……的角度

column1: The lynx has now been reintroduced to the Jura Mountains, the Alps, the Vosges in eastern France and the Harz mountains in Germany, and has re-established itself in many more places.
column2: 如今，人们已把猞猁重新引入汝拉山脉、阿尔卑斯山脉、法国东部的孚日山脉和德国的哈尔茨山脉；它也已经自行在更多地方重新站稳了脚跟。
column3: has now been reintroduced|如今已被重新引入
column8: re-established itself|自行重新建立种群

column1: The European population has tripled since 1970 to roughly 10,000.
column2: 自1970年以来，欧洲的猞猁数量已增至原来的三倍，约为一万只。

column1: As with wolves, bears, beavers, boar, bison, moose and many other species, the lynx has been able to spread as farming has left the hills and people discover that it is more lucrative to protect charismatic wildlife than to hunt it, as tourists will pay for the chance to see it.
column2: 和狼、熊、河狸、野猪、野牛、驼鹿以及许多其他动物一样，随着农业退出山地，猞猁得以扩散。人们还发现，保护这些惹人喜爱的野生动物比猎杀它们更赚钱，因为游客愿意花钱观赏。
column9: charismatic wildlife|极富吸引力的野生动物

column1: Large-scale rewilding is happening almost everywhere — except Britain.
column2: 大规模的再野化几乎到处都在进行，英国却是例外。

column1: Here, attitudes are just beginning to change.
column2: 在英国，人们的态度才刚刚开始改变。

column1: Conservationists are starting to accept that the old preservation-jar model is failing, even on its own terms.
column2: 自然保护人士开始承认，即便按照旧模式自己的标准衡量，那种把自然装进密封罐里的保护模式也正在失败。
column4: preservation-jar model|密封罐式的保护模式
column6: on its own terms|按其自身标准衡量

column1: Already, projects such as Trees for Life in the Highlands provide a hint of what might be coming.
column2: 苏格兰高地的“生命之树”等项目，已经让人窥见未来可能出现的变化。
column4: Trees for Life|“生命之树”项目
column6: provide a hint of|让人窥见

column1: An organisation is being set up that will seek to catalyse the rewilding of land and sea across Britain, its aim being to reintroduce that rarest of species to British ecosystems: hope.
column2: 一个新组织正在筹建，将致力于推动英国各地陆地和海洋的再野化。它的目标，是把那种最稀有的“物种”重新引入英国的生态系统——那就是希望。
column7: rarest of species|最稀有的物种
